## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Otaraṇahārasampāta* ("Conveying Ways of Entry: Combined Treatment") is a section of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 31) in the late Khuddaka/sutta collection. It represents the combined or synthetic exposition (*sampāta*) of the *otaraṇa-hāra*, the interpretive mode or "way of entry" through which doctrinal elements are examined in relation to core Buddhist categories [DharmaNexus].

In discussions of doctrinal categories within the *Netti*, this treatment of *otaraṇa* illustrates the principle of reciprocity among the requisites of awakening (*bodhipakkhiyā dhammā*), explaining that while the four establishments of mindfulness (*satipaṭṭhāna*) are being cultivated, the four right efforts (*sammapadhāna*) and subsequent sets reach fulfillment because all dhammas contributing to awakening share the single characteristic of leading out [Gethin 2001].

 However, DharmaNexus records extensive Pali-internal text reuse, identifying 106 matching passages across seven Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest textual alignment within the *Netti* itself is with its companion analytical section, the *Otaraṇahāravibhaṅga* (Ne 15), sharing 30 matches totaling 4,691 characters (notably Ne 31 §2.3–6.1 aligning with Ne 15 §8.1–12.1) [DharmaNexus]. It is also heavily cited and expounded in the commentary *Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* (30 matches) and the subcommentary *Nettivibhāvinī* (37 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Additionally, it shares recurring structural and transitional formulas with other *sampāta* chapters of the *Netti*, including the *Lakkhaṇahārasampāta* (Ne 24), *Āvaṭṭahārasampāta* (Ne 26), *Yuttihārasampāta* (Ne 22), and *Adhiṭṭhānahārasampāta* (Ne 33) [DharmaNexus].
